target_customer: Programmers and hobbyists building simple web apps in JavaScript
problem: Writing and hosting a web application required setting up servers and stacks. AppJet offered an in-browser editor and hosting using JavaScript on both client and server.
business_model: free hosted development platform, no revenue model found
product_category: online web app development platform (later collaborative editor EtherPad)

founders.name: David Greenspan
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page, which says AppJet was founded by former MIT students.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ran user apps on a custom Java-based virtualization system with the Rhino JavaScript engine, allocating CPU time and cutting off greedy apps.

defensibility.rationale: The platform was not a durable moat and the team shut free hosting in 2009; EtherPad's real-time collaboration engine was the valuable asset and was later open sourced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google bought AppJet on 2009-12-04 for the EtherPad team to join Google Wave, then released the EtherPad code as open source on 2009-12-17.

market_need_then: Developer interest in simple hosted web app tools was present in 2007, but the team found more traction with the EtherPad demo app, which was seen as a threat to Google Docs.

identity.logo: not described by any source found

branding.brand_signature: The EtherPad product, which outlasted the AppJet name
branding.community_and_virality: EtherPad drew wide press and invite demand in 2009 and its code was open sourced after the acquisition.

brand_strength.rationale: AppJet itself had little brand awareness; EtherPad was the better known product name.

pivots.why: Free hosting was discontinued effective 2009-07-01 and the founders focused on EtherPad, per search coverage.

outcome_analysis: AppJet entered YC in Summer 2007 with a hosted JavaScript platform, launched a public beta in December 2007, then pivoted toward its EtherPad real-time editor demo. After closing a roughly 250 thousand dollar angel round led by Mitch Kapor in 2009, Google acquired it on December 4, 2009 to join the Wave team and later open sourced the code.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503. Angel round amount is from a TechCrunch snippet with no second outlet; stage set to other because the source calls it an angel round. Seedtable lists 700K and 15K and CB Insights 270K, all aggregator figures. Other cofounders (Aaron Iba, JD Zamfirescu) are named in search coverage but not on the YC page, so they are not listed. Price undisclosed; a 10M estimate appeared unconfirmed. No dated 2007 competitor sources found.
